response.justification: The candidate is an experienced senior generalist software engineer with 15+ years of experience, but the profile is almost entirely web, backend, and full-stack development (TypeScript, Node.js, DLang, Ember, React). The role requires native-level Japanese proficiency, which is absent from the candidate's language list (English, Romanian, basic German) — this alone is a hard disqualifier. Additionally, there is no evidence of embedded firmware, LAN-switch, Linux kernel modification, or network security experience (MACsec, 802.1X, NETCONF, SNMP, switch chip SDKs). C experience is limited to a brief stint at National Instruments over a decade ago. Strong engineer, wrong role.
strengths: 15+ years of professional software development, well above the 3+ year bar
Some C/C++ background (National Instruments LabWindows/CVI, Linux/Jack audio thesis project)
Strong engineering practices: TDD, CI/CD, testing tooling, Linux and Docker familiarity
concerns: No Japanese language proficiency — hard requirement for the role
No embedded firmware, LAN-switch, or Linux kernel source modification experience
No network security domain exposure (MACsec, 802.1X, NETCONF, SNMP, L2/L3 switching)
